title: Linear mixed model
biology: Evolutionary biologists follow larval growth under two diets.
design: 36 larvae measured at weeks 0–3; diet assigned to larvae.
question: Does diet change the mean growth slope?
null: The population growth-slope difference between diets is zero.
options: (week | larva) fits larval intercepts and slopes
treatment * week tests different diet trajectories
lmerTest uses Satterthwaite degrees of freedom here
assumptions: Enough subjects; inspect convergence and singular fits
parametric: Model residual variance or time correlation when needed
Use ML for likelihood comparisons of different fixed-effect models
nonparametric: A cluster bootstrap resamples whole larvae
Friedman would answer a simpler complete-block rank question
practice: What does the random slope add beyond a random intercept?
code_simulate:
set.seed(2106)
d <- expand.grid(week = 0:3, larva = 1:36)
d$treatment <- rep(rep(c("Control", "Enriched"), each = 18), each = 4)
intercepts <- rnorm(36, 0, 2.3); slopes <- rnorm(36, 0, .7)
d$mass <- 12 + 2 * d$week + .8 * (d$treatment == "Enriched") +
  .9 * d$week * (d$treatment == "Enriched") + intercepts[d$larva] +
  slopes[d$larva] * d$week + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 1.1)
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
p <- ggplot(d, aes(week, mass, color = treatment)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = larva), alpha = .23) +
  geom_point(alpha = .35, size = 1.6) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#246A73", "#B7663E")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:3) +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "Larval mass (mg)", color = "Diet",
       caption = "Thin lines: individuals; thick lines: observed group means") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16)
print(p)
code_analysis:
fit <- lmerTest::lmer(mass ~ treatment * week + (week | larva), data = d)
summary(fit, ddf = "Satterthwaite")
trend_ci <- confint(fit, parm = "treatmentEnriched:week", method = "Wald")
generating_model: 36 larvae (18 per diet) are measured at weeks 0–3. Mass = 12 + 2 × week + 0.8 if enriched + 0.9 × week if enriched + a larval Normal(0, 2.3²) intercept + a larval Normal(0, 0.7²) slope × week + independent Normal(0, 1.1²) error. Simulated intercepts and slopes are independent. Repeated values share both effects; no rounding.
generating_truth: The control slope is 2 mg/week; enrichment adds 0.9 mg/week. The diet-by-week null is false. Simulated random-intercept and slope SDs are 2.3 mg and 0.7 mg/week.
teaching_point: Random intercepts describe starting differences; random slopes describe trajectory differences.
